Technical Depth Diagnoses complex RAC, Clusterware, ASM, Data Guard, SQL performance, storage, interconnect, OS, backup, and recovery problems. Technical Leadership Acts as a primary escalation point, mentors engineers, reviews designs, raises standards, and influences application and infrastructure decisions. Execution Leads complex initiatives end to end, aligns stakeholders, manages dependencies, and drives permanent corrective actions to closure. Communication Explains technical tradeoffs, communicates clearly during incidents, and keeps risks, ownership, dependencies, and timelines visible. Automation and Standards Builds repeatable automation, CI/CD practices, runbooks, monitoring, and golden paths that reduce toil and failure risk. Key Responsibilities Oracle RAC Platform Ownership Administer and improve Oracle RAC, Grid Infrastructure, Clusterware, ASM, services, SCAN/listeners, and interconnect configurations. Performance and Incident Leadership Lead performance analysis using AWR, ASH, ADDM, SQL Monitor, execution plans, SQL Trace, TKPROF, and OS/storage diagnostics. Diagnose Cache Fusion, GC waits, workload placement, connection storms, cluster instability, storage latency, and interconnect issues. Serve as the technical escalation point for critical incidents, lead stabilization and RCA, and drive permanent corrective actions. Engineering Influence and Shift-Left Reliability Partner with application teams on SQL, indexing, partitioning, schema design, bind usage, connection pooling, transaction boundaries, and resilient failover behavior. Establish database design reviews, deployment guardrails, developer guidance, and production-readiness standards. Automation and Observability Automate provisioning, validation, patching, maintenance, backup checks, DR exercises, health checks, and recurring remediation using Python, Shell, Ansible, Terraform, or similar technologies. Improve Oracle observability using OEM, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Datadog, Splunk, or comparable tools; define actionable service indicators and objectives. Strong Oracle performance tuning and diagnostics experience using AWR, ASH, execution plans, SQL Trace, and Linux diagnostics. Experience with patching, upgrades, migrations, backup/recovery, DR exercises, and controlled production change. Strong Linux/Unix systems troubleshooting skills. Hands-on automation using Python, Shell, Ansible, Terraform, or comparable tooling. Strong technical leadership, mentoring, incident communication, and cross-functional execution skills. Preferred Qualifications Oracle Exadata, OCI, Cloud@Customer, AWS, or hybrid Oracle deployment experience. Application Continuity, FAN, TAF, FSFO, Far Sync, GoldenGate, GDS, TDE, ZDLRA, or advanced Oracle HA capabilities. Database schema CI/CD using Liquibase, Flyway, Bytebase, or comparable tooling. Oracle certifications or relevant SRE/cloud architecture credentials. Expected Outcomes in the First 6-12 Months Establish measurable reliability, MTTR, patching, backup/recovery, and DR-readiness baselines and deliver material improvement. Automate high-frequency and high-risk operational workflows, prioritizing safety, maintainability, and auditability. Establish a practical database architecture and production-readiness review process with measurable adoption by application teams. Deliver documented capacity, lifecycle, resiliency, and corrective-action plans for critical RAC environments. What This Role Does Not Include This is not a people-management role unless separately assigned; leadership is expected through technical direction, mentoring, and execution ownership. This role does not own application code or business logic, although it influences database-impacting application design. The role does not assume unlimited or last-minute DBRE capacity; work must be planned, prioritized, communicated, and committed through the appropriate process. Work Expectations and Location This role requires working during U.S. Eastern Time (ET) business hours and participating in on-call support as required.
